title: Cells and organelles
summary: Who does what inside a cell, and how do they work together?
cards.0.p: According to cell theory, all living things are made of cells, and the cell is the unit of structure and function in living things. Every cell comes from a cell that already existed. Robert Hooke first gave the cell its name in 1665.
cards.0.svg#0: 1. All living things are made of cells
cards.0.svg#1: 2. Cell: unit of structure and function
cards.0.key: Every cell comes from a cell that already existed.
cards.0.once.soru: Where does a new cell come from?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: Every cell forms when an existing cell divides. This is one of the basic principles of cell theory.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: Pasteur's experiments showed that life does not arise on its own from nonliving matter.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: Food gives the cell building blocks and energy. But a new cell forms by division.
cards.1.p: Prokaryotic cells, such as bacteria, have no membrane-bound nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles. Their DNA floats free in the cytoplasm. In eukaryotes, such as plants, animals and fungi, the DNA is inside a nucleus. The cell membrane, ribosomes and DNA are found in both cell types.
cards.1.key: Prokaryote means "before the nucleus", and eukaryote means "with a true nucleus".
cards.2.p: The cell membrane surrounds the cell and chooses which substances go in and out. That is why the membrane is called selectively permeable. The jelly-like fluid that fills the cell is called cytoplasm. Organelles and many reactions are found in the cytoplasm.
cards.2.once.soru: What does the membrane around a cell do?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.yazi: Chooses what goes in and out
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: The membrane is selectively permeable. It takes in what is needed, sends out wastes and keeps harmful substances outside.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.neden: If the membrane let everything through, it couldn't protect the inside of the cell.
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: If the membrane let nothing through, the cell couldn't take in food or get rid of wastes.
cards.3.p: The nucleus is surrounded by a double membrane with pores. Inside are DNA and the nucleolus, which helps make ribosomes. DNA decides which proteins are made. That is why the nucleus is the cell's control center.
cards.3.key: The information in DNA is like the cell's instruction book.
cards.3.once.soru: Mature red blood cells have no nucleus. So what can't they do?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: Before a cell divides, it must copy its DNA. A red blood cell with no nucleus has no DNA to copy. Red blood cells live about 120 days, and new ones are made in the bone marrow.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: A red blood cell carries oxygen with hemoglobin. Having no nucleus makes room for more hemoglobin.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: Blood flow carries red blood cells. This has nothing to do with the nucleus.
cards.4.p: A ribosome is a structure without a membrane, and it makes proteins. Rough ER has ribosomes on its surface. It makes and carries proteins that will be secreted. Smooth ER makes lipids, and in the liver it makes harmful substances harmless.
cards.4.key: Rough ER is the protein production line. Smooth ER makes lipids and neutralizes harmful substances.
cards.4.once.soru: A cell makes a lot of protein. Which structure does it have plenty of?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: Ribosomes make proteins. In cells that secrete, rough ER is highly developed.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: A vacuole stores substances. It does not make protein.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: The centrosome organizes the spindle fibers during division. It does not make protein.
cards.5.p: The Golgi apparatus modifies proteins coming from the ER, packages them and sends them where they need to go in vesicles. So it is like the cell's shipping center. A lysosome is a vesicle that buds off the Golgi and is full of enzymes. It breaks down food and worn-out organelles.
cards.5.key: The Golgi is the cell's shipping center, and the lysosome handles digestion and recycling.
cards.6.p: Mitochondria make ATP from food by aerobic respiration, and their inner membrane is folded. Chloroplasts in plants use light energy for photosynthesis and make glucose. Both organelles have a double membrane and their own DNA.
cards.6.svg#4: both double-membraned, with their own DNA
cards.6.key: The chloroplast turns light energy into food, and the mitochondrion passes the energy in food to ATP.
cards.7.p: A peroxisome uses the enzyme catalase to split harmful H₂O₂ into water and oxygen. Plant cells have three kinds of plastids. Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis, chromoplasts give color, and leucoplasts store starch.
cards.7.once.soru: Hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) foams when poured on a wound, because an enzyme in the tissue splits it into water and oxygen. Why does the cell do this?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: H₂O₂ damages the cell. Catalase in peroxisomes splits it right away into water and oxygen. The released oxygen makes the foam.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: The cell gets its energy from food in the mitochondria. The purpose of this reaction is to protect the cell.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: Very little water is released. The goal is to destroy the harmful substance.
cards.8.p: A plant cell has a cell wall made of cellulose, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole. An animal cell has none of these. Instead, an animal cell has a centrosome that organizes division.
cards.8.key: The membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, ribosomes, ER, Golgi and mitochondria are found in both cells.
cards.8.etk.soru: Tap the numbers. Which structures are in both cells, and which are in only one?
cards.8.etk.noktalar.0.acik: The cell wall is made of cellulose. It supports and protects the plant cell and keeps it from bursting when it takes in water. Animal cells don't have one.
cards.8.etk.noktalar.1.acik: Using chlorophyll, the chloroplast captures light energy and makes glucose by photosynthesis. It is found in plants and algae, not in animal cells.
cards.8.etk.noktalar.2.acik: The central vacuole stores water, nutrients, pigments and wastes. When full of water, it keeps the cell firm. Vacuoles in animal cells are small.
cards.8.etk.noktalar.3.acik: The nucleus holds DNA and runs the cell. Plant and animal cells both have one.
cards.8.etk.noktalar.4.acik: The centrosome organizes the spindle fibers when the cell divides. It is found in animal cells. Plant cells build their spindle without a centrosome.
cards.8.etk.noktalar.5.acik: Mitochondria make ATP by aerobic respiration. They are found in both plant and animal cells.
cards.8.etk.noktalar.6.acik: The cell membrane is a selectively permeable boundary found in every cell. In plants, it lies just inside the cell wall.
cards.9.p: A food vacuole carries food, and the food is digested when it fuses with a lysosome. In freshwater organisms, the contractile vacuole uses ATP to pump out extra water. The central vacuole in plants stores water and keeps the cell firm.
cards.9.key: If a paramecium is put in salt water, less water flows in, and its contractile vacuole slows down.
cards.9.once.soru: Water keeps seeping into a paramecium living in fresh water. What does it do to keep from bursting?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.yazi: It pumps out the extra water
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: The contractile vacuole uses ATP to pump out the extra water that seeps in.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: If it stored the water, it would swell and burst.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: Water would still seep in. The solution is to pump the extra water out.
cards.10.p: The cytoskeleton gives the cell its shape and moves vesicles around. The centrosome organizes the spindle fibers during division. Cilia and flagella make movement possible. Cilia are short and many, and flagella are long and few.
cards.10.key: Ribosomes and centrosomes have no membrane. The nucleus, mitochondria and chloroplasts have a double membrane. The other organelles have a single membrane.
cards.10.once.soru: A sperm cell swims to reach the egg. Which structure does it use?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: A sperm swims by whipping its long flagellum.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: Animal cells have no cell wall. A cell wall doesn't provide movement either.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: A vacuole stores substances. It doesn't provide movement.
cards.11.p: A protein that will be secreted passes along a production line: ribosome and rough ER, Golgi, vesicle and finally the outside of the cell. The vesicle fuses with the cell membrane and releases the secretion outside. This is called exocytosis. Mitochondria supply the energy needed.
cards.11.svg#0: Route of a secreted protein (e.g., insulin)
cards.11.key: In cells that secrete, rough ER and the Golgi are highly developed.
cards.12.p:
• The cell is the unit of life. Prokaryotes have no membrane-bound nucleus, and eukaryotes do.
• The nucleus runs the cell. Ribosomes and ER make products, the Golgi packages them, and lysosomes digest.
• Mitochondria make ATP, and chloroplasts make food. Peroxisomes break down H₂O₂.
• Plants have a wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole, and animals have a centrosome.
• The contractile vacuole pumps out extra water.
quiz.0.q: A salivary gland cell makes and secretes the enzyme amylase. Which organelle plays no direct part in this?
quiz.0.e: Amylase is made on ribosomes and carried through the rough ER to the Golgi. The Golgi packages it and sends it out in a vesicle. The lysosome handles digestion inside the cell and is not part of the secretion line.
quiz.0.y.0: Ribosomes on the rough ER make and carry the secreted protein. This is the first stop on the line.
quiz.0.y.1: The Golgi packages the secreted protein and sends it to the cell membrane in vesicles.
quiz.0.y.3: Every protein is made on ribosomes. Amylase is a protein too.
quiz.1.q: Match each structure with its job.
quiz.1.ciftler.2.1: Splits H₂O₂ into water and oxygen
quiz.1.e: Mitochondria make ATP, and lysosomes digest inside the cell with their digestive enzymes. Peroxisomes break down H₂O₂ with catalase, and smooth ER makes lipids. The contractile vacuole pumps out extra water that enters by osmosis.
quiz.2.q: Sort each structure by the cell it is found in.
quiz.2.e: The cellulose wall, chloroplasts and large central vacuole are found only in plant cells. Mitochondria, ribosomes, the Golgi and the cell membrane are found in both.
quiz.3.q: Sort each structure by the cell type it is found in.
quiz.3.e: The only membrane structure in prokaryotes is the cell membrane. The nuclear membrane and membrane-bound organelles are unique to eukaryotes. Ribosomes, the cell membrane, DNA and cytoplasm are found in every cell.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Find the organelles, switch to a bacterium and a plant cell, and follow insulin's route.
A:adimlar.0.metin: This is an animal cell. Inside it are organelles, each doing a different job. In hard-working cells like muscle, one of these organelles is especially plentiful.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.soru: Which organelle makes ATP from food?
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The Golgi packages and ships proteins. It doesn't make ATP.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Mitochondria break down food with oxygen and pass its energy to ATP. Muscle cells use a lot of ATP, so they have many mitochondria.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A lysosome is a vesicle full of digestive enzymes. It doesn't make ATP.
A:adimlar.1.metin: Worn-out organelles and food taken into the cell need to be digested. Small vesicles full of enzymes do this job.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: Which organelle digests inside the cell?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The nucleus holds DNA and runs the cell. It doesn't digest.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A ribosome is a structure without a membrane that makes protein. It doesn't digest.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The inside of a lysosome is acidic, and digestive enzymes work only there. The lysosome's membrane keeps these enzymes apart from the rest of the cell.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Now switch to a bacterium and compare it with the animal cell.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: Which one is found in a bacterial cell?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Every cell has to make protein. So ribosomes, which have no membrane, are found in every cell.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A mitochondrion is a membrane-bound organelle. Prokaryotes have no membrane-bound organelles.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A bacterium's DNA floats free in the cytoplasm with no membrane around it.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Now switch to a plant cell and find the differences.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: Which one is found in a plant cell but not in an animal cell?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The strong cellulose wall keeps a plant cell from bursting when it takes in water and swells. Animal cells have no such wall.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Plant cells need ATP too. Mitochondria are found in both cells.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The Golgi packages proteins in both cells.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Turn off the light and look at two organelles in the plant cell.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: Which is found in a plant cell?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: A plant makes its food in chloroplasts. But it needs mitochondria to get ATP from that food. At night, photosynthesis stops, but respiration goes on.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: See what happens when you turn off the light. The plant lives at night too, and its mitochondria make ATP.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A plant cell makes its own food. That is what its chloroplasts are for.
A:adimlar.5.metin: A pancreas cell makes insulin and secretes it into the blood. For this job, the organelles work together like a production line.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: What route does insulin follow until it leaves the cell?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The order is backward. The protein is made first on a ribosome and shipped last from the Golgi.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The protein is made on a ribosome on the rough ER and packaged in the Golgi. A vesicle fuses with the cell membrane and releases the insulin outside.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The lysosome digests. It is not on the route of a secreted protein.
A:kapanis.0: The cell is the unit of structure and function in living things. Prokaryotes have no membrane-bound nucleus or organelles, and eukaryotes do.
A:kapanis.1: Ribosomes are found in every cell and make protein. The nucleus runs the cell with the information in DNA.
A:kapanis.2: Rough ER and the Golgi make and package secreted proteins. Lysosomes digest inside the cell.
A:kapanis.3: Mitochondria make ATP from food, and chloroplasts make food with light. Plant cells have both.
A:kapanis.4: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole. Animal cells have a centrosome, and lysosomes are seen mostly in animal cells.
